segments.text: I'm going to hand it over. Everyone, my name is Brandy, obviously from the slide there. I'm going to hand it over to Huma.
Good evening. Bonsoir. Bonsoir.

How are we doing? Good, thank you. So I'm trying to use my big voice already in a big tone so that I make sure that I communicate this very important information to everyone. Can everyone hear me? Great.

So we have spent, some of us spent about four days here. Some, just a little bit few. But where did we come to get here? If we recall on the first day, we got an agenda that was telling us on the route that we were taking to get to the last day.

And today, we just want to remind you a little bit that we have told you on the first day that before coming here, we as a team reviewed over 25 documents from across the global, the regional, and policies sometimes, also that has been implemented at country level. We had three sub-regional consultations where we have, of course, have virtual consultations with national and regional midwives. Some of them are midwifery associations, partners, to develop the priority actions that we have been validating here.

So these documents that we've been validating here is not something that we just thumbs up, but it was through those regional consultations in the African continent. We had one consultation in North Africa, Western Central Africa, Southern Eastern Africa. Then we also developed a prioritization survey, which we shared with the regional participants, of course, to prioritize the actions from these regional consultations that we have done.

So we came through a couple of steps before we got into this room. So, Randy is going to tell us what happened the first day, yesterday and today, before I guide you on what is the next steps. Thank you.

So, we started today with 61, sorry, we started three days ago with 65 draft action. These were from different accelerators. So we had, in total, we had 88 breakout tables and seven shortlisted, sent back 39 actions.

So, we had our breakout sessions, which you were all a part of. It was very cool to go around and see the conversations that we're having, the debates that were happening, and also what you brought back to us for changes and things that made more sense to you and your region. Then we did a tally.
So we tallied both the overall votes. We also tallied the ranking. From there, we took it to the review committee.

So, we were in the basement for lunch and dinner, and we were looking at all of your feedback. And this included not just the ranking, but the comments of how they could be done better, how it could be worded better, or often there was a lot of combinations of actions as well. So the review committee did this, collated, and then, of course, we brought back your validation vote, which I know you've heard a lot about.
So, thank you for everyone for doing that survey. Before I go into it, I just wanna stop and thank everyone. We had facilitators that volunteered to come to the tables and facilitate the tables.

We all know that getting 10 or 12 people to agree on five things can be difficult, but also exciting. I also wanna thank the reviewers who gave up, as I mentioned, their lunch and their evenings, and then, of course, you to the participants for spending literally hours these three days. So can we give a big round of applause to all of you? So, now we're gonna go into the results, and I apologize in advance.

We were tallying this quickly in the basement, and so the slides aren't that pretty. Also wanted to make sure that we had our French and English on there, so I will go through these. Don't worry, I will not read everyone.

So I'm gonna start with Accelerator 1. So we started with Accelerator Run, and we started with the 10 actions, which I know everybody is very familiar with at this time. From there, we narrowed it down to five actions. We had a combination of action one and two.

We had action three, four, eight, and 10. From the survey, if it was 70% of respondents rated at seven, eight, or nine, then we considered that this was a shared collective validation, and also feedback to us that these are what are very important to you to move forward. So from Accelerator 1, we have these four actions.

I also wanna note that in some of these, for example, this one in particular, action four had a lower vote, but there was also recommendations about how we could improve it, potentially reword it. So we will go back. We obviously haven't had time to go through all the comments, but over the next week, we're gonna go back through those comments and see if potentially a rewording or something more specific can help that action be something that can be proposed.
So just know that that is kind of the next steps. We'll talk more about that. Action two, we started with eight.
Sorry, Accelerator 2. We refined it down to five, and as you can see, we have four that have been validated. So we have action one, action three. Action five was not.
Action six, which had a 91.1. So it's nice to see these very high numbers. It shows us how aligned we are in this room. And then, of course, action eight.
Accelerator three, that was our big one. We had 11 for that one. We were able to narrow it down to six, and we're happy to say that all six were validated with quite high scoring.
So we have action one, action two. See, there's a lot of combinations in here. We combined action three and four, combined action seven, combined action eight and nine, and combined action 10 and 11.

And just so you know how we combine that is often there would be two to five or even six tables sometimes that would give recommendations on combinations and how we can make it more specific and to your region or to this region or anything. So that was really the goal. And that's why you'll see quite a number of combined actions.
Accelerator four, we started with nine. And we brought it down to six. And as you can see, we had a high number of validation there.
So we have action one, action three, action four, five, seven, and eight. I'll leave that up for a minute. See lots of photos and eyes on the screen.
Five, we came in with 10 as well. And this one we did go down to seven. And I think a big thing of this too is some of those conversations of what to bring forward and whatnot.
Often we had ties, we made sure we brought more. So this one had a couple more. And then you'll see very clearly the ones.
I think this might be our highest score. So I'm gonna read it. Action six, provide midwives opportunities to participate in higher level decisions, including representations on boards or councils.

96.4%. Accelerator six, we started with 10 on this one as well. We brought it down to five. So the ones that we were able to validate were action one, two, four, five, and six, which did not pass the 70% score.
And action nine. Let everyone take a minute to look at those. Only one more left, my friends.
Okay, action, accelerator number seven. We had seven, two lucky sevens that came forward for original actions. And we put forward five, and we were able to validate all five.
Thank you, this was a survey that we just did. So thanks everyone for doing that. Another really high score for the combination of one and two doing communications campaigns and advocacy.
Let everyone take a look at those. If I can get the next slide. Thank you, so I'm gonna pass it back to you.

And thank you again, everybody, for your time and your effort. I think this is a strong echo of how collaborative we have been, and also how many shared, oops, sorry, it's gone back to me, go back. How many shared actions we have in this room, please.

I think the work we have done, all of us deserves more than that clap. Can we try again? Thank you. Thank you so much for everyone who has made use of their mobile devices or any other way they have made it to voting, because this is what we wanted to hear.

We wanted to make sure that your voices are counted. And now I'm just going to take you through what are the next steps from now on. So we know that after today, we'll have a technical, we have a technically validated roadmap from the country delegations, including many midwives from countries across the African continent.

Is that true? Yes, right. So what we're going to do from here, we are going to add text under the prioritized activities to ensure that we link them to the reference documents and also explain what actions are involved using the comments and additions from the final surveys and collected data. So this is to say, all the comments that you have made during the voting and all the other information that you've provided has not gone unnoticed.

Even those actions that were marked with some comments, we will still incorporate them and put the information that is important under those actions where it's relevant. The second step is that we will develop indicators for each action for periodic review and also so that the roadmap is put into actions and evaluated by member states. So this is not going to be remaining our document that you're going to keep somewhere else, but you remain part of this because the implementation take place at the country level, right? The third step is to manage review and it's our management reviews and approval from partner organizations.

You have seen throughout this process here, we've been having our partners here. So we are going to share this document with our partners to review and also give us a thumbs up for us to go ahead. We will edit and design and then share it back to many of us who will be accessing our emails to ensure that this group still have a final clearance before this become public.
And then lastly, somewhere next year, we will launch it. We'll look for that significant event where we are going to launch this. So the work does not stop here.

We are still calling you that whenever, whichever room that you are going to find yourself from now on, please let us keep the voice rolling because we know what the Midwest of Africa and the partners and the supporters have prioritized during the past three days. And I think that was my work. Absolutely, thank you.

So I please want everyone to stand up and applaud yourselves. We had 65 draft actions, 34 were validated and they're all going into one roadmap. So can I have everyone stand up and applaud each other for all the hard work that you've done at this forum.
